gaps.summary: Target-host startup and prior-version journal/lease migration evidence must accompany a real deployment.
gaps.disposition: Source-level installed-process and distinct-source-artifact rollback is covered by the current installed-process contract and the historical RELEASE-PAIR-001 closure in the fixed pre-cleanup register linked by docs/GAP-REGISTER.md. Actual target-host systemd, identities, network policy and deployment-specific prior-schema approval remain external evidence; no live deployment was attempted.

gaps.summary: Native generation checkpoint/tail recovery and disk-backed permanent command lookup are implemented with lineage-sealed active tails and explicit downgrade export.
gaps.disposition: CLOSED. Canonical native startup consumes a digest-bound selected generation, bounded hot replay and the lineage-bound active tail instead of repopulating all historical commands into the coordinator. V2 sealing carries a compact simulator economic checkpoint (positions, admitted-order count and order-ID watermark) so normal simulator restart restores checkpoint plus bounded tail rather than replaying permanent event history; legacy/V1 upgrade reconstructs that checkpoint only during stopped-state maintenance. Historical `(agent, session, command)` identity and canonical request hashes remain in pinned cumulative disk indexes used by status/admission lookup. Current V2 send-attempt indexes are globally ordered by account/domain/time and use stream merge; a legacy unsorted parent is migrated with bounded external-sort chunks rather than whole-file materialization. Verification streams cumulative indexes. Stopped-state `rebase` can collapse a verified lineage into one parentless generation, publish it crash-safely and only then prune unreferenced ancestors, preserving complete logical events and permanent command/send indexes. Installed-process cost-curve acceptance measures restart recovery, Execution peak RSS, seal cost and retained disk bytes across increasing history and re-verifies an ancient duplicate without resend after rebase. No command identity is expired and PAPER/LIVE authorization remains false.

gaps.summary: Ruleset 22597364 still enforces two approvals, code-owner review and merge queue despite owner-operated intent.
gaps.disposition: OPEN. The read-only transition planner preserves the actual required checks, deletion and force-push protection. The available GitHub integration exposes Ruleset readback but no administrative Ruleset write action; no alternate administration plugin is connected. Server administration and post-change readback therefore remain a real owner action and are not represented as a source-code closure.

gaps.summary: Required callback, quote/snapshot age, Broker reconciliation, reconnect/refresh and exact network-policy source producers are implemented; baseline IB collection and state/integrity alerting are executable.
gaps.disposition: OPEN. Coordinator lock wait/held/outside-venue/total timing and 41 fixed local reason bins are implemented. IB PAPER emits one lock-bound authoritative observation plus native callback ingress lag/conflict, quote/snapshot age, successful post-fill Broker reconciliation duration, reconnect duration and reconnect authoritative-refresh duration. The installed reporter and `ib-paper` collector publish fixed-cardinality textfiles; the supplied Prometheus/Alertmanager rules now cover IB collector/freshness failure, incomplete authoritative state, pending reconciliation, callback conflicts, missing producer families and unknown quote/snapshot age without inventing numerical SLOs. `hepta_broker_egress_policy.py --observe-json` independently performs exact privileged nftables readback and recognizes only canonical allow or compiled deny-all; it is deliberately not sampled by the unprivileged daemon. Complete upstream per-reason lifecycle and portfolio notional/PnL/drawdown are a separate next-stage capability, while actual privileged policy-observer scheduling, target-host collection and real receiver delivery remain external host evidence.

gaps.summary: Actual target-host multiday stability, failure collection and delivery to the real operator remain unverified.
gaps.disposition: Split from the external operations portion of OMS-LIFECYCLE-002 without claiming completion. Disposable PID1, multi-UID process fixtures and loopback monitoring are independent source evidence, not an activated target-host collector or a real receiver. The source-side IB state stream has bounded collection and atomic publication, but the actual target host still has to run it, retain failure evidence and deliver an alert through an approved operator receiver. No host, credential, network policy or trading authority was changed.
